question: A sugary drink was said to restore willpower. Which famous psychology findings held up when many labs repeated them?
answer: Willpower as a fuel tank looked solid in small studies, not large ones. Kurzban showed the brain's glucose use barely changes with mental effort, far too little to drain a tank, and merely rinsing with sugar water seemed to help, which no fuel could explain. A 23-lab replication in 2016 found almost no effect.
move: Test a tidy metaphor against the measurement it implies.
ask: When I say I have no willpower left, is that true, or have I just stopped wanting to?

items.note: Self-control runs down, and glucose refills it.
items.verdict: 23 labs, 2,141 people: the depletion effect was close to zero.

items.note: A number just seen drags your estimates.
items.verdict: Replicated strongly across 36 samples in Many Labs, 2014.

items.note: Standing like a superhero raises testosterone.
items.verdict: With 200 people: no change in hormones or in risk-taking.

items.note: Saying lives saved or lives lost flips choices.
items.verdict: Replicated in Many Labs: same odds, different words, different choice.

items.note: A glimpse of a flag shifts political views.
items.verdict: Across 36 samples in Many Labs, no effect.

items.note: A paid ticket makes people sit through a bad show.
items.verdict: Replicated in Many Labs: money already spent still pulls.
